transcript_turns.content: Fluxpoint just announced HIPAA compliance certification, closing the one gap that has kept Ridgeline out of healthcare deals, but Ridgeline's own compliance work is 4 months from complete. Meanwhile, Lanternq is winning greenfield developer teams on setup speed, a segment Ridgeline has historically owned. Where do you focus the platform roadmap for the next two quarters?

My call is to split the 9-person platform-infra team unevenly: 6 engineers on finishing compliance, 3 on cutting setup time, rather than an even split or an all-in bet on either side.

Here's my reasoning. First, the market read: healthcare deals average roughly triple Ridgeline's typical deal size, but the two comparable enterprise sales cycles took 9 and 11 months, so a healthcare push this half doesn't show revenue for a long time regardless of when compliance finishes; Fluxpoint's HIPAA win doesn't close that door faster, it just makes Ridgeline's 4-month gap visible to prospects sooner. Second, Lanternq's 6-minute setup versus our 22 minutes has already cost 3 greenfield deals in two quarters, and that segment is one we've historically owned, so leaving it fully unattended risks a second front opening while we chase healthcare.

I'd defend the position even against the VP of Sales's read that healthcare is the bigger prize: bigger deal size on paper is not the same as bigger near-term revenue once the 9-to-11-month sales cycle is priced in, and the board's growth plan naming healthcare as a target vertical is a next-year bet, not a this-half fire.
